nextRevision.basis: Rule 4 of the Code on Wages (Andhra Pradesh) Rules, 2026 (G.O.Rt. No. 124 of 29 June 2026) has the VDA revised before 1 April and 1 October every year, and the Commissioner of Labour declares the price index points in force from those dates (notification G/3186486/2026 of 23 March and of 28 September 2026); the contract labour sheet says the October 2026 VDA is payable until 31 March 2027. So the next VDA is due on 1 April 2027. Beedi making's index is declared once a year, from 1 April. The basic wages change only when the government revises a notification.

tables.title: Factories: any manufacturing process
tables.appliesTo: Any manufacturing process in a factory under section 2(m) or section 85 of the Factories Act, 1948, that no other notification covers. Industries with a notification of their own, such as engineering, chemicals, steel, food processing and garments, follow theirs; see every scheduled employment below.

zones.name: All of Andhra Pradesh
zones.areas: One rate for the whole state.

tables.vdaNote: G.O.Ms. No. 4 of 7 January 2012 fixes the basic wages, linked at 847 index points, and a VDA rate per point for each level: ₹12.15 highly skilled, ₹9.80 skilled, ₹8.05 semi-skilled, ₹6.85 unskilled. From 1 October 2026 the index is 1,958 points, so the VDA is 1,111 points at that rate.

tables.title: Contract labour
tables.appliesTo: The wages the Commissioner of Labour fixes for contract labour under rule 25(v)(b) of the A.P. Contract Labour Rules, 1971 (G.O.Ms. No. 11 of 2012), linked to the same price index as the scheduled employments. A contract worker in a scheduled employment is also owed that employment's minimum wage.

verification: Where the documents are. The Labour Department's site (labour.ap.gov.in) renders in the browser; its notices, acts and wage sheets are links in its app bundle, served from api.apfd.apcfss.in. Every source here was downloaded on 22 October 2026 and its SHA-256 recorded.

The VDA notification G/3186486/2026 of 28 September 2026 (Andhra Pradesh Gazette Part II Extraordinary No. 400; 15 pages, English 1 to 6 and Telugu 7 to 15; a scan with no text layer, read page by page). Made under section 7(2) of the Code on Wages and rule 4 of the Code on Wages (Andhra Pradesh) Rules, 2026. Part I lists 65 employments, each with its G.O.Ms. number and date, gazette number and date, and the industrial workers' index points (1982=100) its wages are linked at; the index from 1 October 2026 is 1,958 for all 65. Part II lists five agricultural employments on the agricultural workers' index (1986=100), 1,566 from 1 October 2026. Note (i): the VDA from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027 is for the points above the link points.

The April notification (same file number, dated 23 March 2026, Gazette No. 98 of 25 March 2026, under the Minimum Wages Act) gives 1,923 and 1,527 from 1 April 2026, and lists a 66th employment, tobacco (including beedi making), G.O.Ms. No. 47 of 2006 linked at 483, at 1,904. The October notification does not list beedi making: its index is declared once a year (the department's beedi sheet worked out April 2025 to March 2026 on one index), so 1,904 is taken as in force until 31 March 2027.

Basic wages and rates per point come from the Commissioner of Labour's wage sheets (Excel), one per employment, posted on 4 September 2025 in a folder titled 'Minimum Wages (01-Oct-2025 to 31-Mar-2026)'. Each names its G.O.Ms., gazette and link points, and works the VDA out at 1,886 points. (The sheets' own headings say 'as on 01-04-2025' and 'from 01-04-2025 to 30-09-2025'; the department's contract labour sheet of April 2026 gives 1,886 as the points for 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026, so the folder title is right and the headings were not updated.) Every G.O.Ms. number, date and link point in the 65 + 5 sheets matches the VDA notification's list.
